records.failureSummary: Reviewed src/config/data-dir.mjs (DATA_DIR resolution), src/storage/json-store.mjs (atomic JSON store), src/security/password.mjs (scrypt hasher/verifier), src/server.mjs (bootstrap/logging) and test/ac-04-data-dir-persistence.test.mjs. Verified: (1) user records persisted by the storage layer carry only the caller-supplied fields and the AC-04 test writes exactly {id, username, username_normalized, password_hash, created_at} with no plaintext; the hash string is self-describing scrypt$N$r$p$keyLen$salt$hash with a fresh 16-byte salt per password and never contains the plaintext; (2) no product module logs anything about passwords: password.mjs has zero console calls, server.mjs prints only the data directory path, the bound address and a fixed generic handler-failure string, and hasher error messages never echo the secret or hash; (3) writes go to a uniquely named same-directory temp file with mode 0600, are fsync'd, then published via fs.rename, all serialised through a promise queue, and a fresh module + store instance on the same DATA_DIR reads the record back (AC-04 test 2 green); (4) data/ is empty, .gitignore excludes data/, and the tree contains no committed plaintext test password. Checks: pnpm test = 2/2 pass (both test names carry [AC-04], the only Must AC in this slice), pnpm lint = exit 0. Two concrete defects remain in the storage layer and must be fixed in backend code, so this review routes to a BACKEND follow-up instead of approving: sanitizeUserRecord does not enforce the users column whitelist (a record containing a plaintext password field would be persisted verbatim, leaving the no-plaintext guarantee entirely dependent on the not-yet-written register handler), and writeState only removes the temp file when rename fails, leaking a partial db.json.*.tmp inside DATA_DIR when writeFile/sync fails. Lower-severity hardening items (read-error conflation, missing directory fsync, hash exposure via get-by-id) and test gaps are listed as issues.
